name: Schelling's board: counting 8 or 24 neighbors (like share among the eight around)
description: Schelling's board counting the eight surrounding squares or "the 24 surrounding squares in a 5 × 5 area", equal numbers, half alike wanted, measured on one ruler: the like share among the eight surrounding squares (a wider window dilutes its own count, so each neighborhood's own share would not compare). Schelling (p. 164, stated without a figure): enlarging the neighborhood "attenuates the tendency to segregate, at least for moderate demands and near-equal numbers. This observation may not stand up when less tolerant demands … are put into the larger neighborhoods." Measured (release, seeds 1–20, recorded 2026-09-29): at half alike, 0.80 counting eight and 0.86 counting 24 — more sorting, not less; at a moderate third (the survey's s71.wide.attenuates), 0.66 and 0.55, as he conjectured.
